subject.title: Feature request: Mid-stream message injection (soft steer)

question: Should OpenClaw add an explicit soft-steer lifecycle that interrupts or pauses active generation/tool work, injects user input, and resumes with partial context, or should default steering remain boundary-based?
rationale: This affects shared runtime semantics, channel behavior, transcript/session state, and compatibility with existing steer, followup, collect, and interrupt modes, so source inspection cannot choose the product contract alone.

options.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
options.body: Add a separate command or mode for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for streaming output, tool calls, backend rejection, partial context, and fallback.

options.title: Keep Boundary Steering
options.body: Document current steering as the supported default and limit related work to making messages reliably reach the existing model-boundary queue.

options.title: Broaden Default Steer
options.body: Change existing steer behavior to the stronger lifecycle only after maintainer-approved compatibility and channel/runtime proof.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Soft Steer
recommendation.body: Add a separate command or mode for pause-or-abort, inject, and resume semantics with tests for streaming output, tool calls, backend rejection, partial context, and fallback.

likelyOwner.reason: They are the strongest current-history owner for active-run steering and authored the focused replacement attempt on this lifecycle surface.
